PI is at Caltech; no move found.
PI is on sabbatical through December 2026 and is not taking new students, postdocs, visitors or SURF students.
The Main Page group list names no postdocs. Miki Yun is listed as research staff, so was excluded.
The four students are inferred to be PhD students from the BE and CNS program labels and the 'co-advised' note. The page does not state their year, individual projects or emails.
The roster came from a cached Main Page revision (oldid=27281), so it may be out of date.
PI is still at Caltech according to the BBE profile; no move found.
The people page has no 'last updated' date, so the roster may be outdated.
Member emails are not individually published. The page only states a first-name@caltech.edu convention, so none are listed. Only the PI's email (phillips@pboc.caltech.edu) is published.
Member research focus and year are not on the page, so they are left empty.
Staff on the page, not included in the members list: Heun Jin Lee (Staff Scientist) and Melanie Tiangco (Administrative Assistant).
PI has not moved. She is still at Stanford, with expanded administrative roles. The old Stanford lab page now says the lab has moved to curtis-lab.com.

The people page lists students as 'Graduate Student' without confirming they are PhD students, though the listed programs (Genetics, Cancer Biology, Chemical Engineering) are PhD programs. It gives no years and no emails. Many members have no focus listed.
Four clinical fellows (Marni McClure, Audris Chiang, Colin Bergstrom, Zach Ziheng Xu) are listed under Postdocs. They hold clinical fellow titles, so I left them out of the members list.
The page content comes from a fetch summary. Its date of last update is unknown, so confirm the roster directly with the lab.
The PI's Google Scholar URL was not seen, so it is null.

The PI is now at Arc Institute in Palo Alto. He was named a Core Investigator in September 2023, when he was a UCSF Associate Professor, and he keeps a UCSF appointment. The Arc page lists him as Professor.
goodarzilab.ucsf.edu/people redirected to the Arc Institute home page, so the Arc lab page is the current roster.
The roster page gives no per-member profile links, emails, years or project descriptions, so those fields are null or generic. It also gives no date for the last update.
Staff (Lab Manager Ishwa Muzaffery, Junior Specialist Isabelle Liu) are excluded. A search also surfaced Trey Charbonneau as a research associate, who is likewise excluded.
Arc has advertised a computational postdoc position shared with the Konermann lab.
New program: DeepMind cancer-discovery PhD student researcher placements (Azizi team)
Reports from July 2026 say DeepMind dissolved the AlphaFold team, and John Jumper left for Anthropic in June 2026. Leadership and team structure are in flux.
I did not verify the current organisation of the AlphaGenome team or its leads, and I am not naming AlphaGenome leads.
The student researcher deadline is unverified. The official page lists none and secondary sources conflict.
The cancer-discovery placement details come from a secondary news article about a LinkedIn post, not an official DeepMind page.
Many roles require US or UK location and work authorization, and I could not verify visa sponsorship for a Canadian student.
New program: Scientific Solutions Summer Intern / Analyst
No longer listed: Scientific Solutions Summer Intern

Leadership titles conflict across sources, and a governance database lists other executives (Greg Fisbeck, Ezra Cohen) in science or technology roles. Check the current Tempus team page and SEC filings.
I found no dedicated head of a computational biology or AI-for-science team. The leads listed are company-level executives.
Tempus has no PhD fellowship, residency or visiting program that I could find. Only the summer internships turned up.
The Translational Research and Scientific Solutions entries were not re-opened this check, so their details are carried over from last week.

A first-year student would likely miss the graduation-window requirement in the 2026 PhD internship posting. Check whether the 2027 posting uses the same wording. A visa would probably be needed for a US role.

The careers page (noetik.ai/careers) lists no internship, fellowship, residency, student researcher or visiting programs. It only has 'Express interest' links under AI, Engineering, Data Foundry and Therapeutics.
I found no evidence of an annual intake cycle, so I can't say when a program usually opens. Contact the company directly, or use the Express interest links, to ask about student roles.
The company is hybrid and based in the US. A Canadian student would likely need a visa or work authorization for a US-based role.
The team page gave no individual profile URLs, so profile_url points to the shared team page.
Founder list: the 2023 press coverage names Jacob Rinaldi (Co-Founder and CSO), but he does not appear on the current team page, so I left him out. Leadership may have changed since then.
